<div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12621"/><div sID="gen23291" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12621"/><hi type="bold">3. songs of ... temple--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Amos.5.23">Am 5:23</reference>). The joyous hymns in the temple of Judah (or rather, in the Beth-el "royal temple," <reference osisRef="Amos.7.13">Am 7:13</reference>; for the allusion is to Israel, not Judah, throughout this chapter) shall be changed into "howlings." Grotius translates, "palace"; compare <reference osisRef="Amos.6.5">Am 6:5</reference>, as to the songs there. But <reference osisRef="Amos.5.23">Am 5:23</reference>, and <reference osisRef="Amos.7.13">Am 7:13</reference>, favor English Version.<div eID="gen23291" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23292" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">they shall cast them forth with silence--</hi>not as the Margin, "be silent." It is an adverb, "silently." There shall be such great slaughter as even to prevent the bodies being buried [Calvin]. There shall be none of the usual professional mourners (<reference osisRef="Amos.5.16">Am 5:16</reference>), but the bodies will be cast out in silence. Perhaps also is meant that terror, both of God (compare <reference osisRef="Amos.6.10">Am 6:10</reference>) and of the foe, shall close their lips. <div eID="gen23292" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12623"/><div sID="gen23296" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12623"/>5. So greedy are they of unjust gain that they cannot spare a single day, however sacred, from pursuing it. They are strangers to God and enemies to themselves, who love market days better than sabbath days; and they who have lost piety will not long keep honesty. The new moons (<reference osisRef="Num.10.10">Nu 10:10</reference>) and sabbaths were to be kept without working or trading (<reference osisRef="Neh.10.31">Ne 10:31</reference>).<div eID="gen23296" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23297" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">set forth wheat--</hi>literally, "open out" stores of wheat for sale.<div eID="gen23297" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23298" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ephah--</hi>containing three seahs, or above three pecks.<div eID="gen23298" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23299" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">making ... small--</hi>making it below the just weight to purchasers.<div eID="gen23299" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23300" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">shekel great--</hi>taking from purchasers a greater weight of money than was due. Shekels used to be weighed out in payments (<reference osisRef="Gen.23.16">Ge 23:16</reference>). Thus they committed a double fraud against the law (<reference osisRef="Deut.25.13">De 25:13</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deut.25.14">14</reference>). <div eID="gen23300" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12629"/><div sID="gen23310" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12629"/><hi type="bold">11. famine of ... hearing the words of the Lord--</hi>a just retribution on those who now will not hear the Lord's prophets, nay even try to drive them away, as Amaziah did (<reference osisRef="Amos.7.12">Am 7:12</reference>); they shall look in vain, in their distress, for divine counsel, such as the prophets now offer (<reference osisRef="Ezek.7.26">Eze 7:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.3.7">Mi 3:7</reference>). Compare as to the Jews' rejection of Messiah, and their consequent rejection by Him (<reference osisRef="Matt.21.43">Mt 21:43</reference>); and their desire for Messiah too late (<reference osisRef="Luke.17.22">Lu 17:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.7.34">Joh 7:34</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.8.21">8:21</reference>). So, the prodigal when he had sojourned awhile in the "far-off country, began to be in want" in the "mighty famine" which arose (<reference osisRef="Luke.15.14">Lu 15:14</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="1Sam.3.1">1Sa 3:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Sam.7.2">7:2</reference>). It is remarkable that the Jews' religion is almost the only one that could be abolished against the will of the people themselves, on account of its being dependent on a particular place, namely, the temple. When that was destroyed, the Mosaic ritual, which could not exist without it, necessarily ceased. Providence designed it, that, as the law gave way to the Gospel, so all men should perceive it was so, in spite of the Jews' obstinate rejection of the Gospel. <div eID="gen23310" type="x-p"/>

This is their formula when they swear; not "May Jehovah live!" or, "As Jehovah liveth!"
entries.reader_content_plain: 14. swear by the sin of Samaria-- namely, the calves ( De 9:21 ; Ho 4:15 ). "Swear by" means to worship ( Psa 63:11 ). The manner-- that is, as "the way" is used ( Psa 139:24 ; Ac 9:2 ), the mode of worship. Thy god, O Dan-- the other golden calf at Dan ( 1Ki 22:26-30 ). liveth ... liveth-- rather, "May thy god ... live ... may the manner ... live." Or, "As (surely as) thy god, O Dan, liveth." This is their formula when they swear; not "May Jehovah live!" or, "As Jehovah liveth!"
